lead: A hillside neighbourhood around the Turó de la Rovira, with views and a history of community activism.
text: Its name comes from the old farmhouse (masia) of Can Baró, remodelled in 1647 and owned in the 19th century by the Baron of Sant Lluís. In 1869 its owners divided the estate into plots, which gave rise to the neighbourhood, annexed to Barcelona in 1897. Next to the neighbourhood, the Turó de la Rovira anti-aircraft battery, from mid-1937, has been restored, and that space is part of the Parc dels Tres Turons, which the City Council has still to complete.

It spreads over the Turó de la Rovira, with steeply sloping streets and remains of the Civil War anti-aircraft batteries at the top. In the 20th century it received a great deal of immigration and lacked basic services until the 1980s and 1990s; today it is an area undergoing renovation. At 3,405 €/m² and 847 €/month, its prices are moderate. If you are selling, the average sale price is practically in line with the Horta-Guinardó average. Within the neighbourhood, the price of each flat depends on its condition, its floor and its building, so it is best to compare it with nearby sales rather than with the district average. If you are buying, an 80 m² flat costs about 272,000 € on average, and this neighbourhood sits in the middle band of Horta-Guinardó (6th of 11 by price). If you are investing, the average rent is 7% below the district; before deciding, it is worth studying each deal with real figures for purchase, renovation and rental income.
housing: Blocks and houses on steeply sloping streets, with areas undergoing renovation.
